plain.text: Joseph heard that his father was ill and brought his sons, Manasseh and Ephraim. Israel sat up in bed and told Joseph how God Almighty had appeared to him at Luz (Bethel) and blessed him. He said Joseph's two sons would be counted as his own, just like Reuben and Simeon. He remembered Rachel's death on the way to Bethlehem. When Israel saw the boys, he said, "I never expected to see your face again, and now God has let me see your children too." Joseph placed Manasseh, the older, at Israel's right hand and Ephraim at his left. But Israel crossed his arms and put his right hand on Ephraim's head. He blessed them: "May the God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day, the Angel who has redeemed me from all harm, bless these boys." Joseph was displeased and tried to move his father's hand, but Israel said the younger would be greater. He put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh. Israel said, "I am about to die, but God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers."

summary.bigIdea: Jacob blesses Joseph's two sons, putting the younger first, and calls God "my shepherd all my life".
points: Jacob adopts Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh as his own.
He crosses his hands and gives the greater blessing to the younger, Ephraim.
He speaks of "the God who has been my shepherd all my life".
summary.reflection: Looking back, Jacob saw God as his shepherd all his life. Where can you see God shepherding you?
